thread:
maya: Hey @devex — running into an auth/retry oddity with the lightweight Next agent starter. After the first successful request the browser calls start failing with 401s on subsequent tries.
liam: Can you paste the exact snippet and how you're obtaining the token?
maya: Sure — using edge API route + client proxy. Env in .env.local:
```env
NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY=ephemeral_abc123
REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.test
```
maya: Flow is: client hits /api/start -> server gets token from env -> calls Redwood -> returns stream. First call ok, second returns 401 with "token expired" right away.
sam: Are you minting ephemeral tokens or reusing a long-lived one? Edge runtimes often need server-side refresh.
maya: We're reusing ephemeral token across requests in the client (to avoid server roundtrips). Might be the problem but the sample's readme suggests client-side use.
jordan: This smells like an SDK-parity bug — browser/edge SDK should surface predictable retry behavior or at least doc it. Iirc node SDK has an auto-refresh path.
liam: Quick repro: call /api/start twice within 30s in incognito and you'll see the second one fail. We traced headers: second request missing x-rw-ephemeral.
maya: Also the eval harness in the sample app isn't wired to the prompt set — CI shows zero eval runs after bootstrap.
sam: Ugh. So two issues: onboarding doc implies client usage for keys, and the sample's eval harness config is a noop. Both are friction points.
liam: Workaround for now: move token access strictly to server-only env, proxy requests through serverless function, and hold ephemeral refresh there. Not great for the demo but safe.
maya: I'll open a small PR to update the README to recommend server-side refresh for edge and add a note about the eval harness wiring.
maya: PR will include a tiny code patch that checks for x-rw-ephemeral header presence and falls back to server refresh if missing.
devrel-bot: New PR created by maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-lite-agent/pull/42 :eyes:
ops-bot: Deploy preview ready: https://preview.deploy/next-lite-agent/pr-42 :rocket:
liam: I'll add a unit test in CI to assert second request gets a refreshed token and doesn't 401.
maya: Thanks — pinging @sam for quick review once PR is up. If we can merge before Friday we can include it in the next starter release.
sam: Will review today. If we want long-term fix, eng-runtime needs to surface a clear client-edge refresh helper in the JS SDK. Filing an issue now.
jordan: I can draft a short doc section for SDK parity differences (node vs browser vs edge) to add to the devex docs.
maya: Appreciate it. For immediate unblock the PR + README change will help people avoid onboarding friction.
